requirements.statement: measure how the plugin engine grades large (over 8 MiB), slow-body, and streaming HTTP responses in each of the three execution modes — the Cloudflare isolated runner, the Node isolated runner, and in-process — and record each result against the ADR-0004 probe contract

scenarios.name: When a monitored endpoint returns a body larger than 8 MiB, the spike shall record the graded result in each of the three execution modes.
when: a monitored endpoint returns a body larger than 8 MiB
then: record the graded result in each of the three execution modes

scenarios.name: When a monitored endpoint streams its body slowly but completes under the size limit, the spike shall record the measured latency and graded status in each execution mode.
when: a monitored endpoint streams its body slowly but completes under the size limit
then: record the measured latency and graded status in each execution mode

requirements.statement: determine, in each execution mode, whether a probe rejected by a runtime limit (the body-size limit, the subrequest limit, or the CPU-time limit) can be told apart from a network failure or a target error

measure how many monitors one scheduled run can probe on the Cloudflare isolated runner within its per-invocation limits (10 subrequests, 50 ms CPU, 30 s wall time), counting notification deliveries and the per-run configuration re-validation (FR-20) against the same limits, and decide whether a run must be split across invocations

scenarios.name: When one scheduled run probes more monitors than the Cloudflare runner's subrequest limit allows, the spike shall record whether the run fails, truncates, or completes, and how many probes finished.
when: one scheduled run probes more monitors than the Cloudflare runner's subrequest limit allows
then: record whether the run fails, truncates, or completes, and how many probes finished

requirements.statement: confirm whether the plugin scheduler supports the current 5-minute check cadence
record the spike findings in ADR-0004, and either mark it Accepted or revise it and the affected later phases before engine work (Phase 3) starts

scenarios.name: If any execution mode grades a probe differently from the ADR-0004 probe contract, then the track shall revise ADR-0004 before Phase 3 starts.
when: any execution mode grades a probe differently from the ADR-0004 probe contract
then: revise ADR-0004 before Phase 3 starts

requirements.statement: define the public status response (overall and per-site) as one shared, versioned contract that both standalone StatusBeam and the engine plugin produce and the render library consumes

serve the engine plugin's public status, per-site, and badge endpoints with unwrapped response bodies in the same shape as the standalone endpoints, at a documented path mapping from the standalone paths

scenarios.name: When a client requests the plugin's public status endpoint, the system shall return a body that the shared contract accepts with no wrapping envelope.
when: a client requests the plugin's public status endpoint
then: return a body that the shared contract accepts with no wrapping envelope

scenarios.name: When a client requests the plugin's badge endpoint, the system shall return a body that is a valid shields.io endpoint response.
when: a client requests the plugin's badge endpoint
then: return a body that is a valid shields.io endpoint response

requirements.statement: run scheduled checks for every configured monitor inside the plugin, sharding each run's monitors across separate scheduled tasks so every task stays within one invocation's limits, and keep check history and the current status snapshot in plugin-owned storage

scenarios.name: When a monitored endpoint has not finished its response within 10 seconds, the system shall grade that probe down and go on to the task's remaining monitors.
when: a monitored endpoint has not finished its response within 10 seconds
then: grade that probe down and go on to the task's remaining monitors

requirements.statement: compute 90-day per-day uptime from plugin storage with the same results as the standalone rollup for the same check history
send Slack and generic-webhook notifications when a monitor's status changes
accept Statuspage and Sentry inbound webhooks on public endpoints authenticated by a shared secret token

scenarios.name: If no webhook secret is configured, then the system shall reject every inbound webhook request.
when: no webhook secret is configured
then: reject every inbound webhook request

scenarios.name: If an inbound webhook request carries a token that does not match the configured secret, then the system shall reject it without changing any monitor's status.
when: an inbound webhook request carries a token that does not match the configured secret
then: reject it without changing any monitor's status

requirements.statement: show a current-status summary widget on the EmDash admin dashboard

record a probe whose response exceeds the body-size limit as unsupported, exclude it from status and uptime rollups and from notifications, and show a persistent warning on that monitor naming the limit; plan each scheduled task's calls before it starts so it never begins a probe it cannot afford, and leave every monitor unchanged when the runtime still ends a task early

scenarios.name: When a probe fails because the response exceeds the body-size limit, the system shall mark that probe unsupported.
when: a probe fails because the response exceeds the body-size limit
then: mark that probe unsupported

scenarios.name: The system shall assign each scheduled task no more monitors than its call budget covers, counting probes, notification deliveries, and storage calls.
then: assign each scheduled task no more monitors than its call budget covers, counting probes, notification deliveries, and storage calls

scenarios.name: If a probe is marked unsupported, then the system shall not send a status-change notification for that monitor.
when: a probe is marked unsupported
then: the system shall not send a status-change notification for that monitor

scenarios.name: If a probe is marked unsupported, or the runtime ends its scheduled task early, then the system shall leave that monitor's status and uptime unchanged.
when: a probe is marked unsupported, or the runtime ends its scheduled task early
then: leave that monitor's status and uptime unchanged

scenarios.name: The system shall not switch a monitor configured for GET to HEAD to stay under the body-size limit.
then: the system shall not switch a monitor configured for GET to HEAD to stay under the body-size limit

requirements.statement: store the monitor configuration as one YAML document validated by the same core schema as a standalone `status.config.yml`
provide an administrator-only plugin admin page to edit, validate, save, and test the configuration, saving only when it is valid

when: an administrator saves a configuration that fails the core schema
then: show every validation issue with the path of the offending field

scenarios.name: When an administrator saves a configuration that fails the core schema, the system shall keep the previously saved configuration.
when: an administrator saves a configuration that fails the core schema
then: keep the previously saved configuration

scenarios.name: If the stored configuration changed after the administrator loaded the admin page, then the system shall refuse the save and tell the administrator to reload.
when: the stored configuration changed after the administrator loaded the admin page
then: refuse the save and tell the administrator to reload

scenarios.name: If a user who is not an administrator requests the admin page or any of its actions, then the system shall refuse the request.
when: a user who is not an administrator requests the admin page or any of its actions

requirements.statement: provide a Validate action that checks the configuration without saving it

requirements.statement: apply plugin-only validation rules on top of the core schema — rejecting configurations the plugin cannot run and warning about ones it can run only partially

requirements.statement: keep secrets (the Sentry token, the inbound webhook secret, and the Slack and generic-webhook notification URLs) in encrypted plugin settings that are never returned to the browser, separate from the YAML document

requirements.statement: provide status banner, 90-day uptime bar, and per-site detail components that a site imports into its own pages, reading the public status contract from a configurable base URL that points at either the engine plugin or a standalone deployment

scenarios.name: When the render library's base URL points at a standalone StatusBeam deployment, the components shall render the same per-site status as the standalone page.

requirements.statement: provide an opt-in "status" content block that editors can insert into posts, rendered with the same components

requirements.statement: keep the render library and the content block limited to the public status data — no scheduled work, no storage, and no access to engine state
keep every scheduled task within the Cloudflare runner's per-invocation limits, with no more monitors per task than FR-3 measured
verify contract parity at the HTTP level, comparing the plugin's endpoint responses with the standalone endpoints rather than only the data before it is serialized
